title: Tate-twisted canonical projection comparison
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring] with its pulled-back coefficient rings [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], ordinary unbounded internal-module derived functors $Lf^*,Rf_*$ [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull] and existing derived tensor [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom]. Given $f:X\to S$, internal coefficient modules $L_S,L_X$ [def-sfb-diagonal-coefficient-category], and a specified isomorphism $e:Lf^*(L_S[2])\simeq L_X[2]$, define $T_Z(A)=(A\otimes L_Z)[2]$, where $L_Z$ is placed in degree zero. Define the twisted projection comparison
$$\Pi_{f,e,A}:T_S(Rf_*A)\longrightarrow Rf_*T_X(A)$$
as the inverse tensor-shift comparison, followed by the published canonical projection mate (in [def-sfb-proetale-rational-localizing-projection-helpers]) with arguments $A,L_S[2]$, followed by $Rf_*$ of $1_A\otimes e$ and the tensor-shift comparison on $X$. All comparisons are the existing tensor and derived-functor comparisons; $e$ is retained exactly, with no replacement by an unspecified line isomorphism. The unshifted fixed-line tensor functor is the existing definition of [def-sfb-rational-localizing-twist]. The fixed native tensor and shift structures use the shared bundle of [def-sfb-projective-diagonal-pullback].
